Financial figures are from GE's FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0000040545-25-000015), checked against SEC XBRL; the company completed the GE Vernova spin-off on April 2, 2024 and now operates as GE Aerospace. Ownership is from the 2025 proxy (DEF 14A filed March 13, 2025, accession 0001308179-25-000114), as of December 31, 2024. LEADER: Larry Culp (H. Lawrence Culp, Jr., Chairman and CEO) beneficially owned 1,210,834 shares, marked ** (less than 1%), so pctEconomic is null; 1,082,501 of these are held with shared voting and investment power through family trusts or other accounts. HOLDERS: the proxy gives only the 13G filing dates (Vanguard February 13, 2024; BlackRock January 31, 2025; Fidelity February 9, 2024), not the dates the holdings refer to, so asOf is null. Capital International Investors (5.1%) is the fourth 5% holder and is not listed (max 3). STOCK COMP, JUDGMENT CALL: the 10-K's only stated share-based compensation expense is after-tax ($286 million, the XBRL-tagged figure). The pre-tax expense is not stated; the note gives a related income tax benefit of $152 million, and the statement of changes in shareholders' equity shows 'Stock-based compensation 361' (millions) credited to other capital. The after-tax figure is used as reported and understates the pre-tax cost; it is not grossed up. GEOGRAPHY: the 'Total Non-U.S.' subtotal ($21,363 million) is omitted to avoid double counting; non-U.S. revenue was 55% of the total.

footprint.notes: State rows are only the states GE Aerospace itemised in its March 12, 2024 investment release: Alabama (Auburn $54M), Massachusetts (Lynn $30M) and North Carolina (four facilities $46M: Asheville $11M, Durham >$7M, West Jefferson ~$5M, Wilmington $22M). The release says nearly $450M goes to 22 facilities across 14 states but names only these; the other 11 states have no published amount. Greater Cincinnati ($107M) is a metro area spanning Ohio and Kentucky, so it is recorded as a site, not a state row. The release also cites $100M for U.S. suppliers (not by state) and about $100M for international sites in North America, Europe and India (region row, no country split). The March 12, 2025 release (nearly $1B plan) was also read: it itemises sites (e.g. Greater Cincinnati $113M, Muskegon MI $70M, Auburn AL $51M, Huntsville AL $22M, Asheville NC $20M, Durham NC $16M, West Jefferson NC $13M, West Chester OH $14M, Batesville MS $11M, Lafayette IN $5M) but not state totals, so state values would need summing; it was not used, to keep one plan year. The release's 'interactive map' link now shows the 2026 plan and was not used. 10-K: ~53,000 employees, ~28,000 in the U.S. (US country row); manufacturing and service operations at 67 facilities in 22 states and Puerto Rico and 67 facilities in 24 other countries, with no breakdown by state or country.
